To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the explicit prognostic approach for calculating cloud cover in the Global/Regional Atmosphere and Land Prediction System (GRASPES) has been developed and implemented, and that it has improved the simulation of cloud cover and radiation in GRAPES_Gridded Forecast System (GFS) compared with its diagnostic counterpart.

a prognostics cloud cover scheme is more physically reasonable than the diagnostic one, and the former can be adopted to improve the simulation of cloud cover in global numerical weather prediction models.

the PROGCS scheme is implemented into the GRAPES_GPS global middle‐range forecast system, and it is found to be more realistic in simulating cloud properties and radiation processes than the DIAGCS scheme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application and evaluation of an explicit prognostic scheme for cloud‐cover in GRAPES.

the application of a newly developed explicit prognostic cumulus cloud scheme into the Global/ Regional Assimilation and Predict System (GRAPRES) for global middle-range numerical weather prediction system (GRAPRES-GFS) to improve its performance in simulating the cloud cover, radiation, and the related atmospheric fields.
the development of the prognostic cloud cover scheme (PROG-CS) for the Global/Regional assimilation and Prediction System of China Meteorological Administration (GRAPES).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PROGCS scheme is more suitable to be used in GRAPES_GMF than the previous DIAGCS, especially for the simulation of the low and high clouds, the radiation and the cloud cover.
a prognostically calculated cloud cover scheme is better than the traditional diagnostic one.
a prognostics cloud cover scheme is superior to the diagnostic cloud cover scheme in simulating cloud properties in numerical weather prediction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PROGCS is a promising scheme to be used in numerical weather prediction and climate modeling.

a physically based prognostic cloud cover scheme (PROG‐CS) is implemented in the Global/Regional assimilation and Prediction System for global middle‐ range numerical weather prediction (G‐RAPES_GFS).
a prognostically explicit cloud‐cover scheme has been developed and successfully tested in the GRAPES_GFP model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
an explicit prognostic approach is better than the diagnostic approach in simulating cloud‐cover and radiative heating rate, and it should also be used in the weather prediction models.
the PROGCS can be used as an alternative for DIAGCS to improve the simulation and prediction of cloud cover, radiation, and related weather phenomena.
a more realistic cloud‐cover scheme should be incorporated in a numerical model to better simulate cloud‐radiation interaction and improve model performance.
